segs.e: “Mendicants, I will teach you about the gods of the thundercloud host.
And what are the gods of the thundercloud host?
There are gods of the cool thunderclouds,
These are called gods of the thundercloud host.”

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Seated to one side, that mendicant said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā valāhakakāyikānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjatī”ti?
segs.e: “Sir, what is the cause, what is the reason why someone, when their body breaks up, after death, is reborn in the company of the gods of the thundercloud host?”

segs.p: “Idha, bhikkhu, ekacco kāyena sucaritaṁ carati, vācāya sucaritaṁ carati, manasā sucaritaṁ carati.
segs.e: “Mendicant, it’s when someone does good things by way of body, speech, and mind.
‘The gods of the thundercloud host are long-lived, beautiful, and very happy.’

segs.p: ‘aho vatāhaṁ kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā valāhakakāyikānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjeyyan’ti.
segs.e: ‘If only, when my body breaks up, after death, I would be reborn in the company of the gods of the thundercloud host!’

segs.p: So kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā valāhakakāyikānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjati.
segs.e: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the company of the gods of the thundercloud host.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, bhikkhu, hetu, ayaṁ paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā valāhakakāyikānaṁ devānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjatī”ti.
segs.e: This is the cause, this is the reason why someone, when their body breaks up, after death, is reborn in the company of the gods of the thundercloud host.”

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Seated to one side, that mendicant said to the Buddha:

segs.p: “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yenekadā sītaṁ hotī”ti?
segs.e: “Sir, what is the cause, what is the reason why sometimes it becomes cool?”
“Mendicant, there are what are called gods of the cool thunderclouds.

segs.p: ‘yannūna mayaṁ sakāya ratiyā vaseyyāmā’ti, tesaṁ taṁ cetopaṇidhimanvāya sītaṁ hoti.
segs.e: ‘Why don’t we revel in our own kind of enjoyment?’ Then, in accordance with their wish, it becomes cool.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho, bhikkhu, hetu, ayaṁ paccayo, yenekadā sītaṁ hotī”ti.
segs.e: This is the cause, this is the reason why sometimes it becomes cool.”
